## Evidence, scope, and interpretation

This wiki compiles supplied records dated November 2024–September 2026, plus undated notes. Source IDs identify provenance; a reported status remains a source-specific status unless another record documents its resolution. Requests, draft terms, workarounds, planned deployments, and reported usage are not automatically executed commitments or evidence of approved strategy.

### Source authority and limitations

- Executed contracts establish the stated terms for their defined periods and expressly limited amendments. Drafting, execution, record-entry, effective, and term-end dates are distinct. Operational preparation and roster changes do not advance contractual effectiveness. [D024–D044]
- Emails, CRM entries, meeting notes, weekly updates, chats, and assistant digests preserve operational context but sometimes conflict with signed documents or one another. These conflicts remain visible below rather than being reconciled by source recency.
- Some documents lack a `status: signed` metadata field but contain completed execution blocks: Tansley Amendment 1, QFL Amendment 1, Brackenwater’s 2025 renewal, and Tansleigh’s 2026 renewal. Their bodies document execution. [D031][D032][D035][D040]
- Explicitly nonexecuted records are Brackenwater’s October 28, 2025 customer redline, QFL’s December 3, 2025 Amendment 2 draft, and Thornbury’s February 10, 2026 review form, which was never countersigned. [D034][D036][D038]
- Private records include Tobias’s packaging ownership/ramp note, the Zanesville visit, and Dana’s leave logistics. Their private context is material, particularly where ownership was not publicly announced. [D085][D087][D092]
- The North pipeline review has source metadata/path date **2025-09-12**, but its body says **Tuesday, September 16, 2025**, after Brackenwater’s handoff. Both dates are retained. [D079]
- The October 5 digest attributes a roster correction to an October 4 coverage thread; the supplied direct correction email is dated October 3. No October 4 thread is supplied. [D010][D063]

## Seller, company policy, and internal roles

### Seller and product

**Pemberline Systems** supplies **Pemberline Dock**, hosted yard and dock scheduling software. Contract descriptions include gate check-in, dock assignment, carrier appointment scheduling, trailer tracking, dispatcher console, gatehouse kiosk, carrier portal, yard spotter tasks, and APIs; editions and scope vary by account instrument. [D024][D027][D028]

Seller addresses are inconsistent across instruments and should remain source-specific:

| Record | Seller address |
|---|---|
| QFL signed MSA | 440 Commerce Way, Suite 900, Chicago, IL 60606 |
| Brackenwater unsigned redline | 410 Mercer Wharf, Suite 800 |
| QFL Amendment 2 draft | 400 Mercer Waterway, Suite 900 |
| Thornbury signed renewal | 400 Mercer Street, Suite 900, Seattle, WA 98109 |

These are not established as a relocation sequence. [D028][D034][D036][D039]

### Internal roles and decision authority

| Person | Documented role / scope |
|---|---|
| Ruth Calloway | Recipient of regional digests; participated in QFL executive escalation and requested Q3 API incident rollup. Exact corporate title not supplied. [D009][D064][D105] |
| Ilse Varga | North team lead; reassignment authority in coverage correspondence; acting AM for Dana’s accounts during leave. [D014][D063][D070] |
| Hollis Mbeki | Central team lead; former Tansleigh owner; pooled-account and temporary dealer-account coverage. [D054][D085][D116] |
| Dana Okafor | North AM; QFL and Tamsin owner of record after their respective transfers. [D004][D005] |
| Marcus Lindqvist | North AM; Brackenwater and Thornbury owner; onboarding and kiosk hardware work. [D001][D008][D014] |
| Priyanka “Pree” Sundaram | Also Priyanka Sundaram / Pree; Tansley Parcel AM, former Marrow Fieldworks AM. [D007][D054][D066] |
| Tobias Rendle | Tansleigh owner in private May 19, 2025 note; Marrow Fieldworks owner from January 5, 2026. [D085][D003] |
| June Osei-Lark | Deal desk and contracts manager; redlines, signature verification, billing handoffs, and seller signatory on supplied executed contracts. [D014][D024–D044] |
| Anselm Grieve | CFO; discounts **over 10%** require approval. [D014][D031][D034][D036] |
| Samir Patel | Engineering on-call participant in QFL incident chat. [D018] |
| Moss | Assistant preparing digests for Ruth; also scraped initial engineering incident timelines for Q3 reporting. [D009–D014][D105] |

Tansley’s **14%** discount has explicit CFO authorization. QFL’s initial **12%** discount is recorded as Finance-approved. QFL’s proposed **15%** discount was rejected; no approval follows merely from its inclusion in a draft. [D031][D028][D065]

### Marketing and use constraints

QFL’s signed MSA permits its marks only within its branded carrier portal. External press releases, case studies, and public customer lists require **prior written consent in each instance**. Pricing, including the 12% discount and net seat rate, is confidential under that MSA. These are account-specific contractual constraints, not a supplied general marketing policy. [D028]

Customer feedback is licensed for product use under QFL’s MSA, but customer confidential information and data cannot be included in resulting product updates. Anonymous telemetry must not identify QFL, users, terminals, shipping customers, or drivers or permit reverse engineering of customer data. [D028]

## Brackenwater Freight Co.

### Identity, ownership, and buyer roles

Great Lakes LTL carrier headquartered in Toledo, with Toledo and Grand Rapids cross-docks. Dana sometimes used “Bracken.” Dana held the account before the North team existed; the oldest CRM import reportedly said “legacy migration,” and no start date is known. Transfer to Marcus was effective **September 15, 2025**. [D001][D059]

Greg, the night-shift lead, tested the Toledo pilot. Lena Morcant signed the initial order; no buyer title is supplied. AP participated in the billing dispute. [D059][D024][D096]

### Commercial history

| Instrument | Draft / execution / effective | Seats and pricing | Term end |
|---|---|---|---|
| Initial signed order | Nov 1 / Nov 12 / Dec 1, 2024 | 60; $1,700/seat/year; 8% discount | Nov 30, 2025 |
| Customer redline, unsigned | Recorded Oct 28, 2025; no execution | Proposed 75; 15% discount; CFO approval pending | No specific new term dates supplied |
| Executed renewal | Nov 10 / Nov 21 / Dec 1, 2025 | 64; $1,760/seat/year; 8%; gross $112,640; discount $9,011.20; net $103,628.80 | Nov 30, 2026 |

[D024][D034][D035]

The signed renewal changes only its specified quantities, price, discount, and dates; other earlier agreement provisions continue. The unsigned **75-seat/15%** redline is not the current subscription. December’s weekly rounded current ARR to about **$104k**. [D035][D110]

**Disputed renewal date:** February 10, 2026 CRM says **December 31, 2026**. Signed renewal, September account page, and September 28 weekly say **November 30, 2026**. No signed extension to December 31 is supplied. [D051][D035][D001][D118]

### Draft-only operational terms

The October redline proposed Zebra TC77 backward compatibility without firmware upgrades during Tuesday 22:00–Friday 06:00 Eastern peak windows; Toledo Doors 14–38 and Grand Rapids West were named. It proposed a business-day **04:30 Central** SFTP Carrier Dwell & Yard Velocity CSV following an October 14 Milwaukee South Annex Gate B dispute, ticket **PD-88412**, with tractor scan, gate pass, door bump, and seal sign-off timestamps. It also proposed unlimited virtual overflow drop-spots at Kalamazoo, not additional user seats. Hardware language and CFO approval remained unresolved; no signatures were affixed. [D034]

### Operational history and observations

- Initial setup distinguished receiving, outbound dispatch, and evening yard desks; Door 14 and delayed second-shift pickup examples were setup materials, not commercial amendments. User spelling corrections and shared desk labels needed separation from individuals. [D024]
- March 2025: duplicate driver entry, explicitly not a scheduling problem. April: waiting for Toledo Doors 12–18 schedule CSV after west apron repainting. [D100][D101]
- September handoff: Toledo east apron Doors 14–22 pilot, **02:00–06:00** inbound wave, Thursday **15-minute** gate-wait/printer checks; **44182** concerned Door 22 tablet Wi-Fi, suspected local access point. Renewal check-in planned early October. [D059]
- Handoff packet also had two inbound appointments stacked at Door 6 and an unresolved question about moving an already checked-in trailer’s appointment. September 15 notes identify trailer numbers entered in appointment notes rather than the trailer field; two Door 6 examples were searchable by carrier but not trailer. [D009][D106]
- Pipeline review’s Door 8 held trailer looked ready to unload; possible status label or saved-view/filter problem, not resolved. [D079]
- Custom carrier detention export requested in undated North notes. **PD-8812** Driver_Dwell_Summary duplicate trailer-ID CSV bug reported fixed in December. Toledo night-dispatch training on Detention Summary completed by March 2, 2026. [D014][D110][D113]
- September 2026 Door 12 issue: appointment marked arrived while trailer remains in holding lane; supervisor assumes unloading began. Account note attributes it to skipped status sequence during handoff, not scheduling capacity. [D001]
- September 24 call reproduced an afternoon dispatcher’s wrong-date update using a training record: two browser tabs, different dates; yesterday’s appointment edited, update then believed missing. Date banner was easy to miss on small monitor. [D001]
- **BWF-218:** final printed door-list column clipped in portrait; landscape works. Marcus was to send printer settings. Missed-slot report must distinguish missed appointments from drivers outside gate; requested sample fields are appointment time, gate arrival, and door assignment. [D001]
- September 28: split-trailer overnight check-in question; Marcus preparing sandbox recording of bay-status changes. Winter dock schedule and yard-jockey feedback remained preparation items. [D118]

### Billing resolution and unresolved prerequisites

**BILL-212**, opened January 20, resolved January 23, 2026: duplicate January invoices **INV-88310/INV-88311**, same PO, both generated at **02:00**. Felix attributed duplicate to Stoneharrow webhook retry; INV-88311 voided, credit memo and corrected statement posted. January 21 email asked Marcus not to forward either PDF until corrected. February 10 CRM says AP confirmed wire release and dispute fully resolved. [D096][D069][D051]

September pending items: ten-minute afternoon-shift arrival check, print-layout review against actual Toledo setup, missed-slot sample, renewal preparation using **64 seats** while keeping usage separate from shift roster, and draft follow-up email still needing screenshot attachment and send. [D001]

## Quarrendon Freight Lines

### Identity, ownership, and buyer roles

Truckload carrier / cross-dock network in Upper Midwest. September account page calls HQ **Duluth**, terminals **Superior and Fargo**, with heavy third shift. Signed MSA identifies principal operational HQ at **1880 North Terminal Drive, Saint Paul, MN 55101**; draft Amendment 2 instead says **1880 North Terminal Road**. These geographic/address descriptions are not silently unified. [D004][D028][D036]

**Thea Ramaswell**, Director of Yard Operations, is primary contact and customer signatory across supplied QFL contracts. Greg is a lead dispatcher in April 2026 debrief. [D028][D032][D041][D044][D082]

Marcus owned from **January 6, 2025**; formal transfer to Dana effective **June 2, 2025**. Marcus continued day-to-day through **June 30**, stepping back **July 1**, to support expansion work. This overlap is not a later formal ownership transfer. [D004][D056][D086]

Ilse acted during Dana’s **February 2–March 13, 2026** leave; Dana remained CRM owner and returned **March 16**. [D070]

### Commercial history and disputes

| Record | Dates | Terms |
|---|---|---|
| Signed MSA | Draft Mar 10; signed Mar 28; effective Apr 1, 2025–Mar 31, 2026 | 140 seats; list $1,850; 12% discount; net $1,628; gross $259,000; discount $31,080; net annual $227,920; Tier 2; annual advance; Net 45. [D028] |
| Amendment 1 | Draft Aug 11; signed Aug 19; effective Sep 1, 2025 | 185 seats; seats only, no separate yard subscription. [D032] |
| Amendment 2 working draft | Dec 3, 2025; blank signatures and CFO approval | Proposed 15%; explicitly no force absent authorization and execution. [D036] |
| Rejection | Dec 4, 2025 | Email refuses 15%; QFL stays at 12% until renewal talks. December 8 weekly says rejection happened Friday afternoon, a timing discrepancy with Dec 4 email. [D065][D110] |
| Signed renewal | Draft Mar 2; signed Mar 20; effective Apr 1, 2026 | List $1,920; **10%** discount; net $1,728; end Mar 31, 2027; other provisions unchanged. [D041] |
| Amendment 3 | Draft Sep 8; signed Sep 22, 2026; effective Jan 1, 2027 | 230 seats, seats only; other terms unchanged. [D044] |

August 20 chat first reported **180**, then explicitly corrected to **185**; amendment supports 185. September 30 page reports **185 active seats**, not 230 yet. [D016][D032][D004]

**Unresolved discount conflict:** April 9 renewal debrief says discount “stays at **12%**”; signed March 20 renewal says **10%** from April 1. [D082][D041]

**Billing frequency:** October 2, 2025 CFO email authorizes monthly invoicing at roughly **$25k/month**, requesting Stoneharrow schedule update; initial MSA says annual advance. October 1 CRM estimates ARR “just over **$300k**” after amendment. The email does not establish a new seat rate or discount; completed billing-system update is not supplied. [D062][D028][D050]

**Signer conflict:** March 23 digest says March 20 renewal signed by **Ilse (acting) and Thea**, although Dana returned March 16. Executed renewal’s seller signature is **June Osei-Lark**, customer Thea. [D012][D041]

### Contract constraints and service obligations

- Named individual seats; no generic shared/rotating-shift credentials. Permanent reassignment permitted for employment termination, operational role transfer, or leave exceeding **14 consecutive calendar days**. Expansion in minimum **five-seat** blocks by executed addendum, prorated at net rate; initial active-period floor **140**. Fees generally noncancelable/nonrefundable subject to stated remedies. [D028]
- Tier 2 administrators: up to **six**, appointed by Director of Yard Operations. Sev 1: **24×7×365**, human response **30 minutes**, updates **60 minutes**, continuous engineering. Sev 2: Mon–Sat **05:00–23:00 Central**, response **2 hours**, updates **4 hours**. Sev 3: weekdays **07:00–19:00 Central**, excluding US federal holidays, response **8 business hours**. Sev 4: weekdays **08:00–17:00 Central**, response **2 business days**. [D028]
- Monthly uptime **99.5%**. Credits against next invoice based on **1/12 annual fee**, initially **$18,993.33** monthly equivalent: **5%** for 99.00–99.49%; **10%** for 98.00–98.99%; **20%** below 98.00%. Written claim within **30 days** after month end. Below **97% for three consecutive months** can constitute material breach. Scheduled maintenance Saturday 23:00–Sunday 03:00 Central with **48 hours’** notice; customer networks/hardware, third-party integrations, force majeure and permitted suspensions excluded. [D028]
- Net 45; disputes within **20 calendar days**, undisputed amounts still payable, resolution effort **15 business days**. Interest **1.5% monthly** or legal maximum from day **46**. Suspension process after more than **15 days** overdue, delinquency notice and **10 business days** to pay. Emergency security suspension limited in scope, Director notified within **2 hours**. [D028]
- Automatic successive **12-month** periods; noncontinuation election at least **120 calendar days** before period close. Material breach cure **30 days**; insolvency proceeding dismissal window **60 days**. [D028]
- Customer owns data; CSV/JSON exports during term; **30-day** read-only retrieval after conclusion, active deletion within next **15 days**, encrypted backups within **90 days**. Customer responsible for data accuracy and driver-contact consent; prohibited uploads include PCI data, SSNs, driver-license photos, medical certification records and regulated hazmat security plans, with stated UN/NA code exception. [D028]
- Security: TLS **1.2+**, AES-**256**, tenant isolation, SAML **2.0**, MFA, RBAC; annual SOC 2 Type II and penetration-test summary available confidentially once annually on request. Confirmed security incident notice within **48 hours**; annual disaster recovery test; US redundant zones, RPO **15 minutes**, RTO **4 hours**. [D028]
- General liability cap: trailing **12 months’** net fees, initial **$227,920**; confidentiality/security disclosure super-cap **2×**, initially **$455,840**. Indemnities, unpaid undisputed fees, license restrictions, gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud excluded from caps. Contract cross-references mistakenly label excluded claims as §13.3 and super-cap as §13.4; actual headings are the reverse. Consequential losses, detention/demurrage and supply-chain delay costs excluded. [D028]
- Insurance: carrier rating at least **A- VII**; CGL **$1m occurrence/$2m aggregate**, tech E&O/cyber **$5m**, employer liability **$1m**, umbrella **$3m**; cancellation/reduction notice **30 days**. [D028]
- Warranty correction window **30 days** with termination/pro-rata refund remedy if uncorrected material nonconformity. IP mitigation may include replacement or **30-day** termination notice/refund. Illinois law, Cook County venue, jury waiver; CISG/UCITA excluded. Assignment generally requires consent, with affiliate/M&A exceptions and conditions; Pemberline remains responsible for vendors. Signed written amendments required. [D028]
- Notices: June/legal at Chicago address, `legal-notices@pemberline.example`; Thea and general counsel at Saint Paul, `tramaswell@quarrendonfreight.example` / `legal@quarrendonfreight.example`. Email notices require signed PDF/no bounce; Article 12/16 notices also require courier confirmation dispatched within **24 hours**. [D028]

### Adoption, expansion, and operational history

- March contracting: “east receiving” versus Door 6 label mismatch. April: St. Paul Gate 4 logout during Wi-Fi AP handoff, **PD-8841**. June handoff: Door 8 occupied but empty appointment window interpreted as available. [D100][D101][D102]
- May handoff **4419**: Duluth Gate 3 kiosk glitch; July wrap calls **4419** Gate 3 BOL printer lag with patch awaiting confirmation; undated cheat sheet calls **4419** third-shift Door 14 barcode trailer-tag failure, escalated for firmware testing. These descriptions remain source-specific. [D056][D086][D014]
- July 22 QBR: Duluth **100%** on product, Gate 3 second-shift Wi-Fi issue/AP swap planned; Superior off spreadsheet but overrides Doors 8–12 at **05:00**; Blaine night crews lagging in carrier self-check-in, radioing rather than report use. Fully utilizing **140 seats**, requesting **185**; Fargo target before next spring thaw. Needed Blaine logs Doors 1–20, training, seat headcount split. [D078]
- July 23 **PD-4827**: Thea’s locked application login; separate question whether admin login affected by Door 6 permissions error. Duplicate trailer export and revised exception report requested. “Thea’s account” here means login, not a customer entity. [D057]
- August duplicate Door 6 **06:30** arrivals: same trailer entered via kiosk and manually. September roster: old shared inbox invitations; **ND-2846** replacement-address test before bulk resend. **ND-2841** moved appointment persisted in old door filter until refresh; screen recording supplied. September shift-change explanation emphasized scheduled time versus gate arrival and waiting versus door-assigned trailers. [D016][D106][D009][D079]
- October 4 **PD-4492**, Eau Claire Doors 14–18 **04:00** SMS bay assignment failure; routing patch **19:30**, next morning confirmed cleared without manual intervention. October CRM Fargo checklist depended on duplicate-entry examples and shift coverage. [D010][D050]
- Draft-only December configuration: Eau Claire **QFL-EC04** Doors 14–22 heated staging, **45-minute** detention alerts on **22:00–06:00 CST** shift; Duluth **QFL-DL01** cold-start/axle declarations; proposed `QFL_Daily_Dwell_And_Shunt_Summary_v3` at **05:30 CST** business days, no configuration fee, ticket **PD-88412** opened Nov 19. Not an executed operational covenant. [D036]
- December: Saint Paul Door 14 **05:00** cold-weather barcode timeouts; February **NORTH-241** Duluth Door 6 stale print plan; March **4819** Duluth kiosk disconnects at **05:00**, local cache investigation. [D110][D112][D113]
- April: bobtails not marked departed contaminate `Yard Dwell > 4h`; **8841** portal timeout on CSV manifests above **600 rows**, repeated Apr 7 **05:30 CT**, workaround split file. Green Bay Door 9 dock-lock replacement requires new webhook endpoint. Two new night spotters requested **20-minute** tablet/moves/queue refresher Apr 20. Remittance PDF correction needed for AP Friday run. [D082]
- September: **PD-8841** Duluth printer truncates last **two digits** of trailer number on **53-foot** dry-van check-in. Eau Claire second shift reportedly stopped keeping backup Door 14 clipboards. **4912** Superior Bay 14 `Gate_Dwell_Daily` lag open; Dana following up Thursday before Fargo winter schedule lock. [D118][D004]

### November 4, 2025 incident: three conflicting accounts

| Source | Recorded incident |
|---|---|
| Support **SUP-4471** | Superior; opened 06:42, reproduced SUP-11834 Door 7→9 gate-view staleness; malformed trailer reference blocked sync. Isolated message/restarted worker; queue clear 07:26; Thea confirmed normal 07:41; no lost appointments. Validation/bad-message bypass follow-up. [D094] |
| Incident chat | Superior; began about 06:40 local. Investigation mentioned 06:30 UTC deployment, then deadlocked webhook listener. Partial sync about 08:15, duplicates remained; hotfix/replay completed 14:38, closed 14:44. [D018] |
| Nov 6 executive email | **INC-8841**, stale webhook worker after morning deployment; **Oshkosh**, 18 reefers on County Rd M, Doors 4–19 blind **three hours**, second-shift clipboards. Thea accepted hotfix explanation. Credits requested; weekly 15-minute checks through year end; raw dropped gate-in CSV requested before 17:00 CT. [D064] |

Site, cause, duration, identifiers and restoration timeline are disputed. No supplied record reconciles them or documents the final credit amount. November 10 weekly still sought a clean Door 8 follow-up screenshot. [D109]

## Tamsin Cold Chain

### Identity, roles, and ownership

**TCC**, Pacific Northwest refrigerated warehousing. September page lists Tacoma, Spokane, Portland; initial contract names Auburn, Tacoma, Pasco. These are source-specific footprint descriptions, not proof of closures or replacements. [D005][D030]

Marcus → Dana effective **April 14, 2025**, announced April 10 to free Marcus for QFL expansion. October 1 announced transfer back to Marcus for October 6, but October 3 explicitly corrected the company: **Tamsin stayed Dana’s; Orrin moved**. Marcus had held customer introduction unsent after spotting the mismatch. [D055][D060][D063]

Ilse acting AM during Dana’s February 2–March 13 leave; Dana owner of record, back March 16. [D070]

**Buyer-role change in evidence:** March pilot CRM labels CFO **Pavel Ruud** decision maker/final sign-off. May 2 kickoff follow-up identifies COO **Ines Barrow** as real operational decision maker, CFO only budget approver. This preserves distinct source claims rather than simply replacing one label. Initial customer signatory **Henrik Lindahl**, VP Cold Storage Operations; 2026 signatory **R. Vance**, same title. Derek Vance is Tacoma night-shift yard lead. [D046][D047][D030][D043][D093]

### Contracts

- **OF-TCC-2025-0512:** drafted May 12, signed May 30, effective **June 1, 2025–May 31, 2026**. **48 seats**, list **$1,980**, gross **$95,040**, **5%/$4,752** discount, net **$1,881/seat**, annual **$90,288**. Tier **1**. Annual invoice via Stoneharrow on effective date; ACH/wire, taxes excluded. Named users; internal cold-storage use, C-01–C-36 and Daily Reefer Dwell & Shore Power Report. Tenant/SSO before **04:00 PDT June 1**, Auburn North Gate. [D030]
- Renewal drafted May 11, signed **May 27, 2026**, effective **June 1, 2026–May 31, 2027**, **52 seats**. No revised price/discount/SLA stated in the short renewal; prior terms are not restated. September account page continues Tier 1. [D043][D005]
- Pre-go-live **PD-88412** in initial contract concerned Tacoma Dock B temperature-threshold alerts; escalation to Tier 2 Integrations on a later ticket does not itself amend subscription SLA. [D030][D093]

### Operational history and pending work

- March active pilot, Tacoma Doors 4–9 graveyard shift: **4812** gate queue lockout, browser zoom assistance; clipboard until **04:00**. Pre-cool alerts timely for Yakima shuttle. CFO Week 2 dwell export planned. [D046]
- April 22 kickoff: Tacoma-first sensor scope, last-update timestamp for Door 6 stale occupancy, blank status mistaken for free door. Needed disconnect/late-event samples, feed field names and first-pass doors before 30-minute follow-up and end-May order. April weekly adds arrival-window/pre-cool spreadsheet, Doors 1–9 staging, May 1 sandbox target. [D076][D101]
- May 2 COO conversation: two arrivals, one unloading crew, different schedules; appointment sheet/exception notes needed for arrival-change and reassignment walkthrough. June export requested arrival-time rather than carrier sort. [D047][D102]
- **SUP-3920**, August 12 resolved: Tacoma telemetry silent **00:14**, observed around **00:15 PT**, resumed **06:18**; **11 trailers**, Doors 14–28 manually temperature-checked for dairy. Ingestion node `us-west-2b` worker failed credential rotation after local firewall maintenance; restarted **06:17**, cached data backfilled into **RPT-TEMP-774**, confirmed **11:30**. [D093]
- September: chilled versus frozen filtered-view mismatch; ability to spot temperature-zone mismatch before assignment remained open. October correction preserves Doors 4/5 screenshots of post-midnight appointments showing previous shift/date-filter issue. [D009][D063]
- October 3 **22:15** Tacoma Reefer Dwell & Plug-In Duration export stalled after unfiltered range back to **Jan 12, 2025**; engineering cleared queue, October 6 **06:00** digest expected normal. [D010]
- Undated notes: Tacoma reefer temp-check check-in timeout, support patching form. December duplicate ETA-edit SMS attributed to new clerk’s toggle setting. [D014][D110]
